chapter: Later ventures, lodges and San Francisco recollections
title: Studying as a drugless physician but never practicing
summary: He wanted to be an artist until Johnny gave him drums; later he trained at a drugless physicians' college on West Seventh and never practiced.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: School days: grades, teachers and leaving school

blocks.x: Well, I had that in my mind, you know...always had that in my mind but...uh, I, uh, first wanted to be a...I didn't care nothin' 'bout music much because everybody in my family was a musician. See? Every sister and brother was a musician, and I wanted to be an artist, and I could...I could draw with any hand, and beautiful stuff, and so when my brother come home, he started me on drums, and that was the end of the artwork.
And you never pursued the art any more after that?
No. No. Where was it you studied your medical studies?

Here. They had a school over on...it was on West Seventh Street for...you know, those drugless physicians. That's what they were called--drugless physicians. We used a lot of medicine but we used it for...uh, like, say, I reduced tumor on a woman--I have a tube that I insert in her vagina, and the medicine is in the tube, and it flows out like...uh, steam out of a...and that reduces the tumor. See. And hemorrhoids and things like that--we used medicine to reduce them and things but as far as giving prescriptions, we wasn't allowed to do that. We wasn't allowed to do that. But delivering babies--we could do that--and we give all kinds of other things. You know--diet and exercise, and then I went over and took chiropractic for about three or four months to fill in for manipulation.
Is there a name for this medical practice-- other than drugless medicine? Does it have another name?
What was the name of the medical school? Remember?
It's the Drugless Physicians College, I think it was called. It was over there next to the...Westlake Park...school... uh, Westlake Park on West Seventh there.
And after you were certified, you passed the examination, did you ever practice?
That was when you said, instead you opened Music Town?
But you had taken this training with the intention of practicing...

Yeah, yeah, I was offered a lot of partnerships, you know. Thre was three or four fellows in there that opened up, and some of them...I think there's one or two I see in the book--or hear about now--named Dr. Rudy, and he's been in it...have been...ever since, you know, forty-some years. But I uh...there was ten or fifteen that I know was around here that graduated when I did, that was practicing. I don't know whether they still or not; but I never dig practice.
